standards_recognition.explainer: By construction, this agent ships an enforced, re-verifiable governance plane — privileged actions gated by the CCAS tier ladder, immutable HexaRecord audit, a signed provenance chain, and k-anonymised cohort contracts — mapping to the cross-cutting AI-governance standards. Operating in ai-ml-ops, its declared policy implications and vertical(s) additionally engage the domain standards shown (each tagged with what triggered it); the bundle provides audit-ready evidence structure for them — domain substance and certification remain the operator's responsibility.

requirements.requirement: Action restrictions + escalation to a human for high-stakes operations
requirements.mechanism: CCAS tier ladder (metadata.tier_policy) — every privileged action declared with a tier and routed through the ccas_decide gate; T3/T4 park until provenance-verified approval (structured, action-bound, role-scoped, signed) before egress
requirements.honest_note: The ladder + gate + approval-provenance are enforced and re-verifiable, and it is fail-closed: with no approval backend bound (CCAS_APPROVAL_KEY, a CUSTOMER_SLOT) NO approval verifies and gated tiers never release. This is a tier-enforcement interface + fail-closed approval seam, not a finished approvals system — binding a real approval backend (issuing signed, role-scoped, action-bound approvals) and the per-action tier are customer/domain ground-truth (L3).

requirements.mechanism: H_PRIVILEGED_ACTION_DECLARED — an action-emitting node cannot exist without a declared, CCAS-gated privileged_action; forward+reverse checked

Ed25519-signed agent identity + tamper-evident provenance chain + signed file manifest (every delivered file sha256-bound in MANIFEST.json, canonical hash inside the signed conformance); verify_identity.py re-checks the signed conformance AND re-hashes every file before any bundle code runs
requirements.evidence: identity.json; MANIFEST.json; PROVENANCE.json; verify_identity.py; generator.pub / root.pub

requirements.requirement: Software supply-chain integrity (pinned actions, locked dependencies, SBOM, pinned base image)
requirements.mechanism: GitHub Actions pinned to 40-hex commit SHAs + Dependabot (factory-verified at generation); the transitive hash-locked requirements (uv pip compile --generate-hashes, installed with --require-hashes) and full CycloneDX SBOM are MEASURED BY THE FACTORY (bundle-invariant deps) and BORN IN this bundle as SIGNED files in the Ed25519 manifest — measured before export, not by a post-delivery CI bootstrap; the lock's drift marker binds it to the emitted pyproject. Base image is digest-pinned when the factory CI has measured its registry digest — then deploy/base-image.lock is ALSO born-in and SIGNED in the manifest, and Dockerfile/compose/build-image all consume the measured ref (MEASURED_AND_LOCKED) — else tag-based pending that one measurement (MEASUREMENT_READY), the only value the edge generator cannot reach. Nothing supply-chain-related appears after signing (measured_outputs is empty; the shipped workflow is verify-only and re-verifies fail-closed on every run).

requirements.requirement: Built-image provenance (running container traceable to the signed source bundle)
requirements.mechanism: The emitted build chain binds the image to THIS signed bundle at build time: OCI labels resolved from the SIGNED files (agent id, identity sha256, manifest sha256, karta sha256), the pushed digest is captured and Sigstore-attested (actions/attest-build-provenance, SHA-pinned, OIDC — binds digest to repo+commit+workflow run, attestation pushed to the registry), and the binding record is published in the run summary. Re-verification commands ship in docs/verify_built_image.md (label comparison against the local signed bundle + gh attestation verify). Chain: signed source bundle -> digest-pinned base -> locked deps -> built container -> Sigstore-attested image digest.
requirements.honest_note: The binding MECHANISM ships correctly wired and is re-verifiable, and the attestation is produced in the CUSTOMER CI at build time (never an invented digest). It is NOT externally anchored: the build workflow runs the in-checkout verifier and reads MANIFEST.json from the same mutable checkout, so a party controlling the checkout can tamper the source, neutralise the verifier and update its hash in the local manifest with the in-CI precheck still passing. The binding is therefore tamper-EVIDENT, not externally anchored — ARTIFACT_IMAGE_PROVENANCE_BOUND is N/A until an external trust anchor is configured (HexaBox root fingerprint out-of-band; docs/verify_root_fingerprint.md). Fas 3.42.

requirements.requirement: Immutable audit logging of agent actions
requirements.mechanism: HexaRecord logging on every port (H7 + ARTIFACT_HEXARECORD_CALL) — the audit call is present in generated handlers
requirements.honest_note: Presence of the audit call is gated. A durable, access-controlled audit STORE is a deployment concern (L3).

requirements.requirement: Data minimization / anonymization on shared signals
requirements.mechanism: Cohort k-anonymity contract on every MO port (H_COHORT_ANONYMITY, k_minimum >= vertical floor); k-floor derived, not flat
requirements.honest_note: The contract SHAPE and k-floor are enforced. The anonymization implementation is a customer extension point (L3).

requirements.requirement: Consistent performance; no silent degradation / hallucinated action
requirements.mechanism: Fail-closed degradation — SLM-routed nodes fall back to deterministic, contract-valid stubs rather than emitting unvalidated output
Every port carries a schema contract; edge schema compatibility (H4/H12) + per-port contract tests emitted
Port independence (H2) + MacroHub isolation (H_MACROHUB_ISOLATION) — control-plane aggregation cannot reach the primary chain
Doctrine gates re-run at Studio generation, on every PR (CI), and at runtime (CEVE)

nis2_reporting.py + reporting_profiles.py ship the Art 23 filing clock as a pure, unit-tested regulatory layer (early warning +24h, notification +72h, final report). It is NOT composed into the runtime chain in this build
requirements.honest_note: The agent delivers an UNBOUND NIS2/DORA reporting engine and a binding seam — it does NOT yet produce reporting artifacts in the composed runtime chain. module_truth.json records nis2_reporting as generated_unbound with zero runtime importers, and this claim is derived from that record rather than asserted alongside it. Wire the reporting step into the incident flow (REPORTING_PROFILE selects the regime; NIS2_DISPATCH_WEBHOOK the sink) before making any production-tense claim.

requirements.mechanism: CCAS T3/T4 route high-consequence actions to human / dual-approval before execution
requirements.honest_note: Operationalizes / maps to Art 14. Risk-classification of the deployed system is the provider's obligation.

requirements.mechanism: Signed provenance chain + doctrine conformance report + capability truth (implemented vs stub) shipped with every build
requirements.honest_note: Maps to named 42001 controls (documentation, traceability). Certification is an organizational management-system audit.

requirements.honest_note: Never 'GDPR compliant'. The k-anon shape is enforced; the lawful-basis and real anonymization are deployment/organizational (C8).

disposition.why: degraded-mode signalling (truth over green) is invoked by the LLM/SLM binding path — this build has 0 ai_bound nodes, so no caller is wired.
disposition.binding_required: bind a model (llm_binding / model_bootstrap path) — the cognitive nodes then raise the degraded signal instead of running silently green.

disposition.why: binds the distilled SLM client from env; fail-closed by design — with SLM_ENDPOINT unset nothing is bound and the agent stays on the deterministic stub.
disposition.binding_required: set SLM_ENDPOINT (deployment binding) and invoke bootstrap at the entrypoint — the module then binds via llm_binding.set_slm_client.

disposition.why: the NIS2 Art 23 filing clock is a pure regulatory layer; the incident-filing/dispatch step it clocks is a business-flow binding not composed in this skeleton.
disposition.binding_required: wire the reporting step (REPORTING_PROFILE env selects the regime; NIS2_DISPATCH_WEBHOOK for real dispatch) from the incident flow that files reports.

honesty_notes: Language is 'maps to' / 'audit-ready evidence for'. This artifact never claims 'certified' or 'compliant'.

AIUC-1 certification requires accredited adversarial testing (security/safety/reliability) + quarterly re-test. This skeleton provides the enforced governance controls and audit-ready evidence STRUCTURE, not the certification.

Governance plane (gates, tiers, provenance, k-anon shape) is enforced and re-verifiable offline. Domain plane is an honest stub (see capability_truth: implemented vs stub) — domain evidence is customer-supplied (L3).
Score is structural conformance, not domain correctness.
